title: Mid-circuit ground-state cooling and ancilla readout in the $\textit{omg}$ architecture
authors: Sean Brudney, Connor Burns, Gabriel J. Gregory, Evan Ritchie, David J. Wineland, David T. C. Allcock, Jameson O'Reilly
abstract: The trapped-ion optical-metastable-ground ($\textit{omg}$) architecture for quantum processors promises the full functionality of two-species experiments, including sympathetic cooling and non-destructive ancilla readout, without the corresponding hardware overhead. We confirm that we can cool a global motional mode of a mixed metastable-ground state Coulomb crystal to the motional ground state via dissipative operations on the ground ($\textit{g}$) qubit without disturbing coherence of the metastable ($\textit{m}$) qubit. This enables quantum logic spectroscopy to non-destructively readout the state of the $\textit{m}$ qubit using fluorescence detection of the $\textit{g}$ qubit. Extensions of these demonstrations to larger system sizes should enable the mitigation of motional heating after ion shuttling and syndrome extraction for quantum error correction, both crucial primitives for future fault-tolerant quantum computers based on trapped ions.
summary: The paper reports on achieving mid-circuit ground-state cooling in the omg trapped-ion architecture. By using dissipative operations on one qubit species to cool the shared motional mode, they enable non-destructive readout of a second metastable qubit. This capability is crucial for implementing error correction and complex quantum gates in future ion trap processors.
main_problem: The core challenge is demonstrating mid-circuit ground-state cooling and non-destructive ancilla readout within the optical-metastable-ground (omg) trapped-ion architecture.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated cooling the global motional mode to near the quantum ground state ($ ar{n} \approx 0$) while preserving the coherence of the metastable qubit, enabling non-destructive readout for quantum logic spectroscopy.
method: The technique combines measurement-based cooling using dissipative operations on the ground qubit with fluorescence detection on an ancilla ion to read out the metastable qubit state.
model_or_system: The physical system is a trapped-ion crystal utilizing two species: a metastable qubit ($	ext{m}$) and a ground state ($	ext{g}$) ancilla. The process involves complex laser sequences, including Doppler cooling, EIT cooling, and specialized sideband driving for cooling.
key_observables: Motional state occupation number ($ ar{n}$), FC success rate ($99.81\%$), and qubit coherence times ($T_2$).
important_parameters: Cooling fidelity achieved to $ ar{n} = 0.02(1)$; the metastable qubit lifetime is assumed largely undisturbed during short pulses.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the metastable manifold remains spectrally isolated from the fast cycling transitions used for detection and cooling.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the laser beam geometry for two ions, and show the sequence of Doppler and EIT cooling steps alongside heating effects from fluorescence checks or RF displacement.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup, presents measurements on motional excitation sources (FCs, RF pulses), validates the non-destructive readout mechanism via QLS principles, and concludes by confirming ground-state cooling capability for fault-tolerant primitives.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses crucial hardware requirements—cooling and readout fidelity—for scaling trapped-ion quantum computers, providing vital experimental benchmarks for open quantum system control.
